full_story_part2_c1.parent_text: I stood motionless. For an hour he sat in bed, listening. At last he groaned softly. Not pain—terror. I knew that sound. I uncovered the lantern. Its narrow beam found the eye. Wide open. A low, quick beating reached me, like a watch wrapped in cotton. His heart! Faster it went, and louder. What if a neighbour heard? I rushed forward. He shrieked once. I dragged him down and pulled the heavy bed over him. Finally, the beating stopped. I checked his pulse. Nothing. I hid his body beneath three floorboards and fitted them back exactly. Not a mark! You could have searched all night. At four in the morning, three police officers knocked. A neighbour had heard a shriek.

full_story_part3_c1.parent_text: I welcomed them. A bad dream, I explained; the cry was mine. The old man was away in the country. I showed them every room, then brought chairs into his bedroom. I sat directly above the body. You see how little I feared? They chatted pleasantly. I smiled. Then my head began to ache. A ringing filled my ears—but no. That low, quick beating again. I spoke louder. It grew louder too. I paced and scraped my chair across the boards. Still they chatted. Still they smiled. Louder. Louder! Could you have borne it? They heard! They knew! Their smiles were mocking me. I could bear no more. "I did it!" I screamed. "Tear up the planks! Here! It is the beating of his hideous heart!"
